title: Minestrone
intro: Plenty of summer vegetables simmered slowly until the soup turns thick and sweet.

steps.t: Finely chop the onion, carrots and celery. Dice potatoes and courgettes (1 cm), cut beans, shred cabbage, chop tomatoes.
Soften the chopped onion, carrot and celery in 3 tbsp oil over low heat for 8 minutes, until tender.
steps.label: Base

steps.t: Add the potatoes, green beans, cabbage and tomatoes and stir for 3 minutes, until the cabbage wilts.
steps.label: Veg

steps.t: Pour in the hot stock (store-bought, or salted water, is fine) and bring to the boil.
Lower the heat, half-cover and simmer gently for 40 minutes, stirring now and then.
steps.label: Simmer

pressure.t: Lock the pressure cooker lid and cook for 15 minutes at pressure on low heat, then release.

steps.t: Add the courgettes, peas and borlotti and cook 15 more minutes, until the potatoes break down and it thickens.
steps.label: Finish

pressure.t: Open, add the courgettes, peas and borlotti, and cook uncovered for 10 minutes until thick.

steps.t: Season with salt and pepper, turn off the heat, add the torn basil and let it rest for 10 minutes.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Serve hot or warm with a drizzle of raw olive oil.

tips.t: A spoonful of pesto in each bowl makes it minestrone alla genovese (no longer vegan).
For a full meal, cook 150 g ditalini or rice in it for the last 10 minutes (pasta adds gluten).
It's even better the next day; in summer eat it cold, as they do in Liguria.

title: Pasta e fagioli
intro: Partly blended borlotti and ditalini cooked in the soup: creamy without any cream.

steps.t: Finely chop the onion, carrot and celery and soften them in 3 tbsp oil with the garlic and rosemary over low heat.
steps.label: Base

steps.t: Add the passata and chilli and cook for 5 minutes, until it thickens.
steps.label: Tomato

steps.t: Add the beans and hot stock (store-bought is fine) and simmer for 20 minutes.
steps.label: Beans

steps.t: Remove the garlic and rosemary. Blend a third of the beans with some broth and return it to the pot.
Bring back to the boil, add the pasta and cook it in the soup for the time on the pack, stirring often.
steps.label: Pasta

steps.t: If it's too thick, loosen with hot water. Season, turn off the heat and let it rest for 5 minutes.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Serve with a drizzle of raw olive oil and some black pepper.

tips.t: If it needn't be vegan, simmer a Parmesan rind in the broth and lift it out before the pasta.
With dried beans: soak 200 g overnight, then simmer 1½ hours or pressure-cook 25 minutes.

title: Tuscan ribollita
intro: Cavolo nero, beans and stale bread: the farmhouse soup that gets better reheated.

steps.t: Strip the cavolo nero from its stems and shred it with the cabbage. Dice the onion, carrots, celery and potato.
Soften the onion, carrots, celery and garlic in 4 tbsp oil over low heat for 10 minutes.
steps.label: Base

steps.t: Add the crushed tomatoes, potato, cavolo nero and cabbage and stir until the leaves wilt.
steps.label: Greens

steps.t: Mash half the beans and add all of them with the hot stock (store-bought is fine). Cover and simmer 50 minutes.
steps.label: Soup

pressure.t: Mash half the beans, add them all with the stock, lock the pressure cooker and cook 20 minutes at pressure.

steps.t: Thinly slice the bread. In a pot, layer bread and soup, finishing with soup.
Leave to rest for at least 30 minutes, or better overnight in the fridge, until the bread soaks up the broth.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Reheat over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring, until thick enough for a spoon almost to stand up.
steps.label: Reheat

steps.t: Serve with plenty of raw olive oil and black pepper; add thinly sliced red onion if you like.

tips.t: Use unsalted Tuscan bread at least two days old: it holds together and doesn't turn to paste.
It keeps 3 days in the fridge and tastes better every time you reheat it.

title: French onion soup
intro: Long-caramelised onions, beef broth and a cheesy toast melted under the grill.

steps.t: Halve the onions and slice them thinly.
Melt the butter with the oil, add the onions and 1 tsp salt. Cook over medium-low heat for 45 minutes, stirring often, until deep brown.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 2 minutes, until it no longer tastes raw.
steps.label: Flour

steps.t: Deglaze with the wine, scraping the bottom, and boil for 2 minutes until almost evaporated.
steps.label: Wine

steps.t: Pour in the hot stock, add the thyme and bay leaf, and simmer for 20 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Soup

steps.t: Meanwhile toast the baguette slices in the oven at 200 °C for 5 minutes, until dry and golden.
steps.label: Toasts

steps.t: Remove the thyme and bay. Ladle the soup into ovenproof bowls, float two toasts on each and cover with cheese.
Grill at 230 °C for 4–5 minutes, until the cheese bubbles and browns. Careful: the bowls get very hot.
steps.label: Grill

tips.t: Don't turn up the heat to rush the onions: if they stick, add a splash of water and scrape.
Add 2 tbsp cognac with the wine for a deeper flavour.

title: Miso soup
intro: Plant-based kombu and shiitake dashi, silken tofu and miso stirred in at the end.

steps.t: Put the kombu and shiitake in 1 litre of cold water and leave to soak for 30 minutes.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: Heat slowly over medium-low heat. Lift out the kombu as soon as small bubbles appear at the edge, before it boils.
steps.label: Dashi

steps.t: Simmer the shiitake for 5 minutes, then lift them out, slice thinly and return them to the broth.
steps.label: Shiitake

steps.t: Meanwhile soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes and drain. Cut the tofu into 1.5 cm cubes.
steps.label: Wakame

steps.t: Add the tofu and wakame to the hot dashi and warm them for 1 minute without boiling.
Turn off the heat. Whisk the miso into a ladle of broth and stir it back in: don't let it boil again.
Serve right away in bowls, topped with sliced spring onion.

tips.t: Boiled miso loses its aroma and turns grainy: always add it off the heat.
For classic dashi (not vegan), add 10 g katsuobushi after the kombu and strain after 2 minutes.

title: Andalusian gazpacho
intro: Chilled soup of ripe tomatoes emulsified with olive oil: refreshing and filling.

steps.t: Chop the tomatoes. Peel the cucumber, keeping a little aside. Seed the pepper. Peel the garlic and remove any green germ.
Soak the bread in cold water for 5 minutes, then squeeze it out well.
steps.label: Bread

steps.t: Blend the tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, garlic, bread, salt and vinegar for 2 minutes, until very smooth.
With the blender running, drizzle in the oil until the gazpacho turns pale orange and creamy.
Pass it through a sieve for a silky texture. Thin with cold water if thick, and adjust salt and vinegar.
Chill for at least 2 hours: it should be served ice-cold.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Serve in glasses or bowls with diced cucumber and pepper and a drizzle of oil.

tips.t: With 200 g bread, only tomatoes and no water it becomes salmorejo: top with egg and jamón.
Use very ripe tomatoes, even ugly ones: they bring the sweetness and colour.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge in a closed bottle: shake before serving.

title: Turkish red lentil soup
intro: Silky blended red lentils, finished with chilli-mint oil and plenty of lemon.

steps.t: Rinse the lentils until the water runs clear. Chop the onion and dice the carrot and potato.
Soften the onion in 2 tbsp oil for 5 minutes, then add the carrot, potato, tomato paste and cumin for 2 minutes.
steps.label: Base

steps.t: Add the lentils and hot stock (store-bought is fine). Simmer for 25 minutes, until the lentils fall apart.
steps.label: Lentils

pressure.t: Add the lentils and hot stock, lock the pressure cooker and cook for 8 minutes at pressure. Let it release.

steps.t: Blend with a stick blender until smooth. Thin with hot water if too thick and season with salt.
Heat the remaining oil in a small pan, take it off the heat and add the chilli and mint: it should sizzle, not burn.
Serve the soup with a drizzle of the spiced oil and lemon wedges to squeeze at the table.

tips.t: Serve with warm pita or toasted bread to scoop it up.
It thickens a lot in the fridge: reheat with a little water. Freezes well for 3 months.

title: Tom kha gai
intro: Thai chicken and coconut milk soup, sour with lime and fragrant with lemongrass.

steps.t: Bruise the lemongrass and cut into 4 cm pieces. Slice the galangal, tear the lime leaves, slice mushrooms and chicken.
Bring the stock (store-bought is fine) to the boil with the lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves; simmer 5 minutes.
steps.label: Aromatics

steps.t: Add the coconut milk and chicken and simmer gently for 8 minutes, until cooked through. Don't let it boil hard.
steps.label: Chicken

steps.t: Add the mushrooms and crushed chillies and cook for 3 minutes.
steps.label: Mushrooms

steps.t: Turn off the heat and season with fish sauce, sugar and the lime juice. Taste: sour, salty, a little sweet.
Serve with fresh coriander. Lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves are just for flavour: don't eat them.

tips.t: Serve with a bowl of jasmine rice on the side.
Vegetarian version: tofu for the chicken, veg stock, and soy sauce instead of fish sauce.

title: German potato soup
intro: Potatoes, leek and celeriac, only half blended: thick, rustic and scented with marjoram.

steps.t: Peel and cut the potatoes, carrots and celeriac into 1.5 cm dice. Slice the leek and chop the onion.
Soften the onion and leek in the butter over medium-low heat for 5 minutes, without browning.
steps.label: Leek

steps.t: Add the vegetables, marjoram and hot stock (store-bought is fine). Simmer 20 minutes, until the potatoes are soft.
steps.label: Soup

pressure.t: Add the vegetables, marjoram and stock, lock the pressure cooker and cook for 6 minutes at pressure. Release.

steps.t: Blend about half of the soup with a stick blender, leaving some chunks.
Stir in the cream, nutmeg, salt and pepper and heat for 2 minutes without boiling.
steps.label: Cream

steps.t: Serve piping hot, sprinkled with parsley.

tips.t: German-style: warm sliced frankfurters in the soup or top with crispy bacon (no longer vegetarian).
Serve with buttered rye bread.

title: Tom yam kung, hot and sour prawn soup
intro: Prawn broth with lemongrass, galangal and makrut lime: sour, hot and deeply fragrant.

steps.t: Peel the prawns leaving the tails on, devein them and keep the heads and shells.
Simmer the heads and shells in the water for 15 minutes, then strain the broth.
steps.label: Broth

steps.t: Meanwhile bruise the lemongrass and cut into 4 cm pieces, slice the galangal, tear the lime leaves and crush the chilies.
Bring the broth back to a boil with the lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves and simmer 5 minutes.
steps.label: Aromatics

steps.t: Add the mushrooms and halved tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes.
steps.label: Mushrooms

steps.t: Add the prawns and cook for 2 minutes, until just pink and curled. Turn off the heat.
steps.label: Prawns

steps.t: Off the heat stir in the fish sauce, chili paste, lime juice and chilies. Taste: it should be sour and hot.
Serve piping hot with cilantro. The lemongrass, galangal and leaves are only for flavour: don't eat them.

tips.t: Add the lime off the heat: boiled lime juice turns bitter and loses its aroma.
For the creamy version, tom yam nam khon, stir in 100 ml evaporated or coconut milk at the end.
With a bowl of jasmine rice on the side it becomes a full dinner.

title: Harira, Moroccan lamb and lentil soup
intro: Lamb, lentils and chickpeas in a velvety tomato broth: Morocco's Ramadan soup.

steps.t: Chop the onion and celery. In a large pot brown the lamb with the oil, onion, celery and spices for 5 minutes.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Add the rinsed lentils, grated tomatoes, tomato paste, half the chopped herbs and 1.5 l water. Cover and simmer gently until tender.
steps.label: Soup

pressure.t: In a pressure cooker add lentils, tomatoes, tomato paste, half the herbs and 1.5 l water; cook 20 minutes once at pressure.

steps.t: Stir in the chickpeas and vermicelli and cook for 8 minutes, stirring now and then.
steps.label: Vermicelli

steps.t: Meanwhile whisk the flour into the cold water until there are no lumps.
Pour the batter in slowly while stirring and cook for 10 minutes, until the soup turns velvety and thick.
steps.label: Thicken

steps.t: Turn off the heat, add the rest of the herbs and the juice of half the lemon, and salt to taste. Serve with lemon wedges and dates.

tips.t: Leave out the lamb and it's vegan: add an extra 50 g of lentils so it stays hearty.
During Ramadan it comes with dates, hard-boiled eggs and chebakia, honey and sesame pastries.
It thickens as it sits: loosen it the next day with a splash of hot water.

title: Suanla tang, hot and sour soup
intro: Thick broth with mushrooms, tofu and egg ribbons, sharp with vinegar and white pepper.

steps.t: Soak the shiitake and wood ears in hot water until soft.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: Squeeze them out, remove the tough stems and slice into strips. Cut the tofu and bamboo into matchsticks; strain 200 ml soaking water.
Bring the stock (shop-bought is fine) and mushroom water to the boil, add the mushrooms and bamboo and simmer.
steps.label: Broth

steps.t: Add the tofu and both soy sauces. Mix the cornflour with the water, stir it in and cook for 1 minute until the soup thickens.
Lower the heat, beat the eggs and drizzle them in a thin stream while stirring gently in one direction: they form fine ribbons.
Turn off the heat, add the vinegar, white pepper and sesame oil, season with salt and serve topped with sliced spring onions.

tips.t: Add the vinegar and pepper off the heat: if they boil they lose their aroma and punch.
Leave out the eggs and it's vegan: add extra tofu and mushrooms instead.
Like more heat? Add a teaspoon of chilli oil to each bowl.

title: Kenchinjiru, vegetable and tofu soup
intro: Zen temple soup: winter vegetables and tofu fried in sesame oil, in a plant-based dashi.

steps.t: Put the kombu and shiitake in 1.1 litres of cold water and leave to soak for 30 minutes.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: Meanwhile peel the daikon and carrot and slice into thin quarter-moons. Dice the potato and pat the tofu dry.
Heat slowly and lift out the kombu before it boils. Remove the shiitake, cut off the stems and slice.
steps.label: Dashi

steps.t: Heat the sesame oil in a pot, crumble in the tofu by hand and fry with the vegetables and shiitake for 3 minutes.
steps.label: Sauté

steps.t: Pour in the dashi, bring to a boil and skim. Simmer for 15 minutes, until the daikon and potato are tender.
steps.label: Vegetables

steps.t: Season with sake, soy sauce and a pinch of salt and simmer for 2 more minutes.
steps.label: Season

steps.t: Serve piping hot in bowls, topped with sliced spring onion.

tips.t: If you find konnyaku and burdock root (gobo) at an Asian shop, add them: that's the full version.
With classic kombu and katsuobushi dashi it's richer, but no longer vegan.
It's even better the next day: reheat gently, without boiling it for long.

title: Yayla çorbası, yogurt and rice soup
intro: Highland yogurt and rice soup, scented with melted butter and dried mint.

steps.t: Rinse the rice and cook it in the hot stock (store-bought is fine) over medium heat for 18 minutes, until very soft.
steps.label: Rice

steps.t: Meanwhile whisk the yogurt, egg yolk and flour in a bowl until smooth and lump-free.
Temper the mixture with a ladle of hot stock, whisking, then a second one: this stops the yogurt from splitting.
Lower the heat and pour in the yogurt in a thin stream, always stirring the same way. Simmer gently 5 minutes, never boiling hard.
steps.label: Yogurt

steps.t: Season with salt. Melt the butter in a small pan, take it off the heat and add the mint and chilli: let them sizzle 10 seconds.
Ladle the soup into bowls and drizzle with the mint butter.

tips.t: Always stir in the same direction and never let it boil hard: the yogurt stays smooth.
Use cooked chickpeas or cracked wheat instead of rice, as they do in Anatolia.
It thickens in the fridge: reheat gently with a splash of water, without boiling.

title: Pozole rojo
intro: Pork and hominy soup in red chili broth, topped at the table.

steps.t: Cut the pork into 5 cm chunks and put it in a pot with the water, half the onion, 3 garlic cloves, the bay leaves and 2 tsp salt.
Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer covered over low heat until the meat is tender.
steps.label: Pork

pressure.t: Boil and skim, then lock the pressure cooker lid and cook 35 minutes at pressure; release.

steps.t: Meanwhile open the chilies, remove stems and seeds and toast them in a dry pan 20 seconds per side without burning.
Cover them with a generous ladle of hot broth from the pot and let them soften.
steps.label: Chilies

steps.t: Blend the chilies with their liquid, 2 garlic cloves, the other half onion, oregano and cumin; strain.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the sauce, stirring, until it darkens and thickens.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Remove the onion and bay from the pot, shred the meat a little, add the sauce and rinsed hominy and simmer.
steps.label: Pozole

steps.t: Meanwhile finely shred the cabbage, slice the radishes into rounds and cut the limes into wedges.
Season with salt and serve in deep bowls: everyone adds cabbage, radish, oregano, lime and tostadas.

tips.t: Mexican oregano from a Latin shop, crumbled over at the table, gives the authentic aroma.
With chicken thighs instead of pork it cooks in 40 minutes and is just as traditional.
It is even better the next day: keep the soup separate from the raw toppings.

title: Fasolada (Greek bean soup)
intro: Greece's national soup: white beans, vegetables, tomato and plenty of good olive oil.

steps.t: Soak the beans in plenty of cold water (overnight is fine).
steps.label: Soaking

steps.t: Drain, cover with fresh water, bring to a boil and boil a few minutes; drain again.
steps.label: Blanching

steps.t: Return them to the pot with 2 litres water and the bay leaf and simmer.
steps.label: Beans

pressure.t: Put them in the pressure cooker with 1.5 litres water and the bay leaf and cook 15 minutes at pressure.

steps.t: Meanwhile dice the carrots, celery and onion.
Add the vegetables, crushed tomatoes, paste, half the oil and pepper; simmer until the beans are creamy.
steps.label: Soup

pressure.t: Open, add the vegetables, tomatoes, paste, half the oil and pepper, lock again and cook 10 minutes.

steps.t: Salt, pour in the remaining oil and cook a few more minutes until the broth is silky.
steps.label: Oil

steps.t: Remove the bay leaf and serve hot with bread, olives and raw onion.

tips.t: In Greece it comes with Kalamata olives, salted sardines and a slice of feta.
With 2 cans of cannellini you skip the soaking: add them with the vegetables and cook 25 minutes.
A pinch of chili and a handful of chopped celery leaves at the end brighten it up.

title: Salmorejo, chilled tomato cream
intro: Córdoba's cold soup: tomatoes, bread and olive oil blended into a thick, velvety cream.

steps.t: Wash the tomatoes, cut them into chunks and blend with the garlic, germ removed, until liquid.
Pass through a fine sieve to remove skins and seeds.
Cut the crust off the bread, tear it into the tomato and let it soften.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: Meanwhile hard-boil the eggs, cool them in cold water and peel.
steps.label: Eggs

steps.t: Blend the bread and tomato on full speed, pouring in the oil in a thin stream, until thick and pale orange. Add salt and vinegar.
Cover and chill for at least 1 hour: it must be served very cold.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Serve in bowls topped with chopped egg, strips of ham and a drizzle of oil.

tips.t: Pour the oil in slowly with the blender on full: it emulsifies into a cream thick enough to hold a spoon.
Skip the ham for a vegetarian version; in Córdoba it's also topped with tuna or black olives.
It keeps 2 days covered in the fridge and makes a great sauce for boiled potatoes.

title: New England clam chowder
intro: Creamy soup of clams, potatoes and smoky bacon, the way they make it in Boston.

steps.t: Soak the clams in cold salted water so they purge their sand, then rinse them well.
steps.label: Purge

steps.t: Cook the clams with the water in a covered pot over high heat, shaking, until they open.
steps.label: Clams

steps.t: Shell them, keeping a few whole, and strain the cooking liquid through a sieve lined with paper towel.
In the clean pot, fry the bacon in the butter, then add the diced onion and celery and cook until soft.
steps.label: Bacon

steps.t: Sprinkle in the flour, stir for 2 minutes, then slowly pour in the clam liquid, stirring.
steps.label: Flour

steps.t: Add the potatoes in 1.5 cm cubes, the thyme and bay, plus a little water if needed to cover; cook until tender.
steps.label: Potatoes

steps.t: Pour in the milk and cream and heat gently without boiling until the chowder thickens slightly.
steps.label: Milk

steps.t: Discard the thyme and bay, stir in the clams, season with pepper and salt to taste. Serve with chives and crackers.

tips.t: Never let it boil once the milk is in: the chowder stays smooth and the clams don't turn rubbery.
Canned clams work too, as many Americans use them: 2 cans with their juice, added at the end.
It thickens overnight: loosen with a splash of milk and reheat gently.
